title: Usage + Quota Sandbox Interaction Proposal
body:
Purpose / overview:

This is a working proposal for a combined "Usage + Quota Sandbox" page that product and console teams can use to: 1) explore per-key and per-route usage breakdowns, 2) preview quota slicing and rate limit effects before applying them to live traffic, and 3) provide debug & export tools for SREs and customer support. The goal is to reduce time-to-triage for quota incidents and to give customers a low-risk way to tune quota and throttle policies.

Context and motivation:
- We repeatedly see CS tickets where customers ask: Why did my key get throttled at 98%? How do I split quotas across product teams?
- Existing per-key/per-route UIs show raw numbers and daily aggregates but do not let users simulate policy changes or easily attribute spikes to routes/models.
- This page aims to sit next to the existing usage charts in Console (not replace), with a heavier focus on causal debugging and safe experimentation.

Primary personas:
- Platform engineers (internal) who need to debug cross-team quota pressure.
- Customer success / support who triage throttle incidents.
- Product engineers at customers who want to preview quota changes before committing.

Key user goals / success metrics:
- Time to first meaningful signal when investigating a throttle reduces from ~30m to <10m.
- Customers run simulation for quota splits before deploying in >20% of quota-change workflows (measured after launch).
- Fewer support escalations caused by unexpected route-level throttles.

Top-level layout (wireframe description):
- Page header: credential selector (autocomplete), route selector (multi-select), timeframe selector (preset + custom), live vs historical toggle.
- Snapshot row (top): single-line quick stats - current tokens/min, 95th latency, error rate %, active routes count, active clients (unique credential ids). Each stat is clickable to reveal the drilldown panel.
- Left column: Interactive timeline chart (combined tokens + throttle events overlay). Hover shows per-route token distribution at each timestamp.
- Right column: Attribution + sandbox controls. Default tab is "Attribution". Tabs: Attribution | Sandbox | Debug logs | Export.

Attribution tab (default):
- Per-route table with columns: route name, model, tokens (24h), tokens % of selected cred, avg latency (p95), throttle count, most-likely-throttle-policy (if any). Rows sortable & filterable.
- Small inline sparkline for tokens to show trend.
- Quick actions on each row: "open trace" (link to tracing), "simulate quota split", "pin to timeline".

Sandbox tab (new interaction):
- Purpose: apply non-destructive policy changes to a local simulation (not live) and immediately see projected outcomes for tokens, throttle frequency, and cost.
- Controls: total quota slider (0–100% of current credential quota) + per-route split drag-and-drop bars. Option to add rules: burst window (tokens/second), priority lane (low/normal/high), fallback route.
- Simulation preview: near-live chart that replays a sampled week of traffic and shows where simulated throttles would have occurred. Shows delta metrics vs baseline: % fewer throttles, estimated cost savings, estimated latency degradation.
- Safety: clearly labeled "Simulation only — no changes applied". CTA button: "Apply policy to live (requires approval)" which opens an approval flow (separate ticket).

Debug logs tab:
- Collapsible feed of throttle reason events (policy id, decision timestamp, matched route, matched credential, bucket usage, trace id if available).
- Filters: reason (rate_limit, quota_exhausted, sla_fallback), region, model, route.
- Option to expand an event to view sampled request headers and prompt hash (PII redacted).

Export tab:
- CSV/JSON export of current table & timeline slice (include raw throttle events).
- Synthetics: sample replay payload for customer to run locally.

Important micro-interactions and edge cases:
1) Credential selector with many keys: support fuzzy matching and show recent/most-searched keys. For org accounts show "team view" to collapse multiple credentials into a single roll-up.
2) If a credential has delegate tokens (sub-keys), allow toggling "include delegated usage".
3) When user pins a route to timeline, the left chart should stack by route to surface multi-route collisions.
4) For very high-cardinality routes, default to top-10 by tokens and provide a "show all" link.

Backlog grooming notes (candidate tickets):
- UX-PRIO: interactive quota-sandbox proto (figma) -> small scope: slider + split bars + replay preview. (PROD-1523)
- ENG-PRIO: backend sampling pipeline for simulation data (store week-sample for each credential). (PLAT-881)
- DATA: attribution engine improvements for route-to-model mapping (handle aliased routes). (DATA-410)
- SRE: add debug consumer topic for throttle events w/ trace ids (for Debug logs). (SRE-223)
- CS: create KB article "Using the quota sandbox" and one-pager for enterprise onboarding. (CS-97)

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy: how much request-level info do we surface in Debug logs? Need to align with privacy/legal; maybe only show prompt hash and redacted headers.
- Simulation fidelity: how accurate will simulated throttles be for burst windows/complex shared capacity? Must set customer expectations.
- Performance: timeline + simulation must be near-instant for small windows; heavier simulations should be async with progress UI.
- ACLs: Who can run simulations vs apply live changes? We need RBAC mapping to teams and admin roles.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Interactive page that shows per-key and per-route table + timeline for selected timeframe.
- Sandbox slider + simple per-route splits with a sampled replay preview for at least 7 days.
- Export of throttle events and per-route CSV.
- Debug logs feed with filter by reason and link to traces.

Design notes / accessibility:
- Use colorblind-friendly palette for route stacking and throttle overlays.
- Ensure keyboard accessibility for the split drag-and-drop controls (allow +/- buttons).
- Tooltips with short microcopy for policy terms (burst window, priority lane).

Prototype links and references:
- Figma: https://figma.com/file/abc123/usage-sandbox-prototypes (early proto)
- Related console pages: per-key-usage (existing), route-latency-dashboard (existing)
- Slack threads: #cs-throttles (internal), #console-ux (for design feedback)

Next steps / immediate tasks (owner assignments):
- Aisha: consolidate this doc into the figma board and create the UX-PRIO ticket (due 2025-01-21).
- Julian: spike backend sample pipeline and estimate storage/cost (due 2025-01-28).
- Rina: draft KB article outline and identify common customer questions (due 2025-02-04).
- Marco: SRE to define event schema for debug logs (due 2025-01-24).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative for launch — focus on high signal actions (simulate, export, pin to timeline). We can add multi-credential rollups and advanced policy grammar in follow-ups.
- Please flag any regulatory concerns about sampled payloads ASAP.

Unresolved UX ideas to revisit later (parking lot):
- Live "what-if" A/B experiments routed to a small % of traffic to validate simulation vs reality.
- Automatically suggested quota splits based on route SLOs and revenue attribution.
- Inline alerts that suggest "consider increasing quota for route X" with one-click apply + audit trail.

Change log:
- 2025-01-14 Aisha: created initial draft and wireframe descriptions.
- 2025-01-20 Julian: added notes on backend sampling and staging limitations.
- 2025-02-03 Aisha: updated acceptance criteria and added export requirements after sync with CS.
